description: Closed-Won Deep Dive Report - End-to-end analysis of all closed-won Code Search opportunities in FY25+FY26, tracing deals from top-of-funnel through close. Python analysis script (pure stdlib) producing structured JSON and self-contained HTML report.

userStories.title: Create script scaffold with data loading and core filters
userStories.description: As an analyst, I need a Python script that loads all six data sources and filters to closed-won Code Search opps in FY25+FY26.
acceptanceCriteria: Create scripts/analyze-closed-won-deep-dive.py using pure stdlib Python (csv, json, re, collections, pathlib, statistics, datetime)
Load sfdc_opportunities.csv, sfdc_account_details.csv, sfdc_contact_roles.csv, sfdc_leads_qualified.csv from data/global/
Load salesforce_notes_product_subset.jsonl and gong_calls_portfolio.jsonl from data/global/
Copy the is_code_search_opp() product filtering pattern from scripts/analyze-pipeline-strategy.py
Copy helper functions: safe_float(), safe_int(), parse_bool(), fmt_currency(), pct() from analyze-pipeline-strategy.py
Filter to is_won == true AND close_date within FY25 (2024-02-01 to 2025-01-31) or FY26 (2025-02-01 to 2026-01-31)
Build lookup dicts: account_details by account_id, contact_roles grouped by opp_id, leads by email
Build lookup: notes grouped by account_id, gong calls grouped by account (join via account_id field if present)
Print summary: total closed-won opps, total iARR, unique accounts, FY25 vs FY26 counts and iARR
Script runs without errors on existing data
userStories.notes: This is the foundation. All subsequent stories add analysis functions to this script. Reference analyze-pipeline-strategy.py for the product filter and helper patterns.

userStories.title: Add lead source and discovery channel analysis
userStories.description: As a marketing strategist, I want to know how closed-won customers entered the funnel so I can allocate campaign budget.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_discovery(won_opps, leads_by_email, contacts_by_opp) that returns a dict
Tabulate lead_source distribution for closed-won opps (count and iARR per source)
Tabulate first_touchpoint distribution
Cross-reference contacts with leads CSV via email to get lead_person_source_category and lead_first_touchpoint
Compute PLG signal prevalence: % of closed-won accounts with product_first_login_private or pql_flg set in matched leads
Compute win rate by lead source using ALL Code Search opps (not just won): won_count / total_count per lead_source
Break down by deal size tier: $0-50K, $50K-200K, $200K+
Break down by FY25 vs FY26
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results in analysis dict under 'discovery' key
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Need all Code Search opps (not just won) to compute win rates. The lead join is via email from contact_roles -> leads.

userStories.title: Add buyer persona and committee analysis
userStories.description: As a sales strategist, I want to understand who the economic buyers and champions are by title and role.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_personas(won_opps, contacts_by_opp, leads_by_email, accounts_by_id) that returns a dict
Count and rank opp_contact_role distribution across closed-won opps
Compute average buying committee size (unique contacts per opp) with median and P75
Join contact emails to leads CSV to get lead_title and lead_title_level
Show top 10 most common titles for Economic Buyer role
Show top 10 most common titles for Champion role
Show committee composition by deal size tier ($0-50K, $50K-200K, $200K+)
Show committee composition by opportunity_type (New Business, Expansion, Renewal)
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results under 'personas' key
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Join path: contact_roles has email -> match to leads which have lead_title and lead_title_level.

userStories.title: Add sales cycle velocity analysis
userStories.description: As a sales leader, I want to know how long deals take to close by segment so I can forecast and find acceleration opportunities.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_velocity(won_opps, accounts_by_id) that returns a dict
Compute median, mean, P25, P75 for days_to_close across all closed-won opps
Break down by deal size tier, opportunity_type, lead_source, fiscal_year, industry (from account details)
Show stage-by-stage median dwell time using opp_days_stage2_to_stage3 through opp_days_stage6_to_won fields
Identify bottleneck stage (longest median dwell)
Calculate POC duration (poc_end_date minus poc_start_date) for opps that have both dates
Show technical_win_achieved rate and median cycle time for technical-win vs non-technical-win deals
Identify 'fast wins' (<30 days) vs 'enterprise slog' (>180 days) with count and median iARR for each
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results under 'velocity' key
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Use statistics.median, statistics.mean. Handle missing/empty stage dwell fields gracefully.

userStories.title: Add technology stack extraction from notes and Gong
userStories.description: As a campaign strategist, I want to know what SCMs, code hosts, and languages our closed-won customers use.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_stack(won_opps, notes_by_account, gong_by_account) that returns a dict
Define regex patterns for SCMs: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Perforce, SVN, Gerrit, Helix Core, AWS CodeCommit
Define regex patterns for languages: Java, Python, Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, C++, C#, Rust, Ruby, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, PHP, R, Objective-C
For Go language: use word boundary pattern that excludes 'go to', 'go ahead', 'let us go', 'going to', 'go with', 'go for', 'go through' etc.
Mine note_text from salesforce_notes for closed-won account_ids
Mine spotlight_brief, spotlight_key_points, transcript_text from gong_calls for closed-won account_ids
Produce per-account stack profile with mention counts
Show frequency table: SCMs ranked by account count, languages ranked by account count
Show top 5 co-occurrence pairs (e.g. GitHub+Java: N accounts)
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results under 'stack' key
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Go disambiguation is critical. Use negative lookbehind/lookahead. Case-insensitive for most, but case-sensitive for Go and R.

userStories.title: Add competitive landscape analysis for won deals
userStories.description: As a competitive strategist, I want to understand who we displaced in closed-won deals and win rates by competitor.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_competition(won_opps, all_cs_opps) that returns a dict
Copy normalize_competitor() and SKIP_VALUES logic from analyze-pipeline-strategy.py
For closed-won opps: count competitor mentions, rank by frequency
Compute win rate per competitor: won / (won + lost) for opps mentioning that competitor (need closed-lost opps too)
Show average iARR and median cycle time for wins against each competitor (top 10)
Cross-tab competitor with lead_source (count matrix)
Cross-tab competitor with use case flags (use_case_code_reuse_flg etc.)
Filter out skip values (TBD, N/A, True-Up, Expansion, etc.)
Handle negative iARR correctly in averages
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results under 'competition' key
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Need both closed-won AND closed-lost opps to compute win rates. all_cs_opps should include both.

userStories.title: Add product mix, use cases, and deal segmentation
userStories.description: As a product marketing manager, I want to understand product bundles, use case patterns, and deal archetypes in won deals.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function analyze_products(won_opps) that returns a dict
Parse products_included field (semicolon or comma separated) to extract individual products per opp
Show product frequency: count of each Code Search product in won deals
Show top 10 product bundle combinations (sorted set of products per opp, ranked by count)

Show use case flag distribution: use_case_code_reuse_flg, use_case_code_health_flg, use_case_dev_onboarding_flg, use_case_incident_response_flg, use_case_security_flg, use_case_dev_productivity_flg, use_case_fixing_vulns_flg
Add function analyze_segments(won_opps, accounts_by_id, contacts_by_opp) that returns a dict
Segment by deal size tier, opportunity_type, industry, region/geo
For each segment show: count, median iARR, median cycle time, top lead source, top use case
Show FY25 vs FY26 trends per segment (count and total iARR)
Print formatted tables to terminal
Store results under 'products' and 'segments' keys
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Products field may be semicolon-separated. Some opps have blank products_included -- use opp name as fallback.

userStories.title: Add JSON output with all analysis results
userStories.description: As a downstream consumer, I need the analysis results in structured JSON for dashboards and follow-on scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: Collect all analysis dicts into a single output structure

Add metadata section: run_timestamp (ISO 8601), filter_criteria (product filter, date range, won filter), record_counts (total opps loaded, total CS opps, closed-won count, accounts, contacts, notes, gong calls)
Add executive_summary section: total_deals, total_iarr, median_cycle_days, top_lead_source, top_competitor_beaten, top_use_case, top_buyer_title
Ensure all numeric values are raw numbers (int/float), not formatted strings
Use snake_case for all JSON keys
Write to data/global/analysis_closed_won_deep_dive.json with json.dump indent=2
Print confirmation message with file path and size
Script runs without errors and produces valid JSON
userStories.notes: Use default=str in json.dump for any datetime objects that might slip through.

userStories.title: Add HTML report generation - structure and styling
userStories.description: As a sales leader, I need a polished HTML report with executive summary, tables, and navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function generate_html_report(analysis_results) that returns HTML string
Self-contained HTML with all CSS inline in a <style> block (no external resources)
Professional color scheme: dark headers, alternating row colors, clear typography
Table of contents at top with anchor links to each section
Executive summary section with headline metrics in a card/grid layout
Each analysis section rendered as formatted HTML tables with headers
Tables support: aligned numbers (right), left-aligned text, highlighted top values
Print-friendly: @media print styles that remove navigation, set white background
Write to data/global/closed_won_deep_dive_report.html
Report opens cleanly in Chrome
Script runs without errors
userStories.notes: Use string formatting/f-strings for HTML generation, no template libraries. Keep it clean and readable.

userStories.title: Add inline SVG charts to HTML report
userStories.description: As a sales leader, I want visual charts in the report for quick pattern recognition.
acceptanceCriteria: Add function render_bar_chart(data, title, width=600, bar_height=24) that returns SVG string
Bar chart: horizontal bars with labels on left, values on right, proportional bar widths
Generate SVG bar chart for: lead source distribution (top 10 by count)
Generate SVG bar chart for: competitor win frequency (top 10)
Generate SVG bar chart for: stage dwell times (stages 2-6 to won)
Generate SVG bar chart for: product frequency (all Code Search products)
Generate SVG bar chart for: use case flag distribution
Charts use consistent color scheme matching the report theme
Charts render correctly in Chrome and in PDF export via print
Insert charts into appropriate report sections alongside the data tables
Script runs without errors and report renders all charts
userStories.notes: SVG uses <rect> elements for bars, <text> for labels. Viewbox-based sizing for responsiveness. No JavaScript.
